column1: # tests/waivers-0.0.43.tsv -- known gaps of 0.0.43, written down so the matrices and the release notes agree (tools/matrix-waive.cx --check).
# 2026-10-31: the owner left the release scope to cc ("你来安排") after a read-only evaluation; each group goes to 0.0.44 as a named requirement.

column3: win/arm64 native entry is C44-WIN-ARM64-01 (0.0.44); 0.0.43 ships the win/x86_64 PE, which runs under system emulation on Windows on ARM; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31
the libunisacc embedding API (us_*) is C44-LIBUNISACC-01 (0.0.44): no live implementation, never part of the public unisacc.com release; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31
macro-expansion diagnostic column and excerpt are C44-DIAG-COLUMN-01 (0.0.44): line is right, column and excerpt follow the expanded text; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

column1: # 2026-10-31 (R4): the stand-alone single-stream container is a non-product build artifact; the installed product cannot take it (grk's study: route names are rewritten to "stream", the product compiles C and rejects bare UNITOK1/USLATTR1, executor budget is a constant, tools/stream-runtime.c needs the archived exec/c/run.c).

column3: single-stream containers (non-product build) are C44-STREAM-CONTAINER-01 (0.0.44): rebuild the stream runtime from the current tree; 0.0.43 ships the five-slice unisacc.com whose per-stream behaviour is covered through the product routes; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

column1: # 2026-10-31 (R5): user malloc under RLIMIT_AS: include/stdlib.h _unisa_map treats only -1 and 0 as failure, raw syscall 9 returns -ENOMEM (-12); the header ships inside the package, so the fix is a new candidate and changes every user image that links the allocator.

column3: user-program malloc returning -ENOMEM as an address under RLIMIT_AS is C44-MALLOC-01 (0.0.44): fix include/stdlib.h _unisa_map (ret<0 is failure) and regenerate include/cx-flat.h via tools/cx-flatten.cx; needs a new package and changes the bytes of user images that use the allocator; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

column1: # 2026-10-31 (R6): the product step budget is a build constant.

column3: the product step budget is the constant 400000000000 in src/executor.cx (pinned at 259 lines by srcshape): exhausting it is not reachable inside the 60 s bound and a named refusal of UNISA_MAXSTEPS values needs more lines in stages/runexec; a configurable, validated budget is C44-BUDGET-01 (0.0.44); the product ignoring UNISA_MAXSTEPS is covered by res.steps.product-env-ignored; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

column1: # 2026-10-31 (R7-R9): stage-level cells that need stage input the product does not accept, a 2^26 boundary, and an unimplemented non-stable diagnostic.

column3: stage-level cells whose input is a stage stream the installed product does not take (UNITOK2 directories, tape text for the assembler, tape for lowering, a stream without credential): they are observable only on stand-alone single-stream containers, C44-STREAM-CONTAINER-01 (0.0.44); the product-visible results of the same stages are covered by the product routes; owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

e3.lim.capacities includes the 2^26 token-span boundary, which cannot be reached inside the 60 s bound; the smaller limits stay covered where they are reachable; a bounded-capacity build for boundary tests is C44-STREAM-CONTAINER-01 (0.0.44); owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

--emit-host-symbols (UNISYM1 sidecar) is a Diagnostic, non-stable flag of 0.0.43: the product accepts it and writes no sidecar; making it real is C44-HOSTSYM-01 (0.0.44); owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31

column1: # 2026-10-31 (R10): the C-prefix record oracle is archived.

column3: the C-prefix (Q-prefix) malformed-record check needed the archived exec/c/run.c and exec/c/qprefixcheck.cx (host cc, Python); its batch negative-model-qprefix is retired; a private re-encoder (re-deflate with a valid CRC) that also serves loader.semantic-illegal-action is C44-LOADER-SEMANTIC-01 (0.0.44); owner delegated the scope to cc 2026-10-31
